parts.label: Part 4
parts.article:
Now turn to section four on page seven.

Section four.

You will hear a university lecturer talking to his students about an architectural studies assignment.

First, you have some time to look at questions thirty-one to forty on pages seven and eight.

Now listen carefully and answer questions thirty-one to forty.

Okay. Before this morning's lecture on successful design of public buildings, I want to draw your attention to your next assignment. So your assignment is on public monuments, and by that I mean any structure or statue that is built to remind us of important events or of historic figures. The assignment should be divided into three sections. At the beginning of section one, you should identify the monument you're examining and say why you've chosen it. Include a comment on whether you think the monument works. By that, I mean its success. You may think it's wonderful. You may think it's a public eyesore, something that people hate looking at.

Next, you should also include in this first section information about where the monument was built, its geographical site, and also a discussion of its social importance, how relevant it was for the people of the time.

You should also include information on when it was built, its historical background, and make sure you illustrate the assignment appropriately too. I shall expect that. Insert any plans you can find and make sure any photographs you use have captions and are clearly referred to in the text, or they will be meaningless.

To end this section, you should include something about the record of the person who designed the monument, showing how the monument relates to his or her other work.

Right. In section two of the assignment, you'll need to give a detailed account of the design and construction of the monument. Firstly, I'll want to read about any particular influence you think is apparent in the design. More often than not, there will be something in it that links it to an established style, classical Greek, for example. Or it may reflect a movement like Bauhaus or Art Nouveau. You decide.

Secondly, I want information about the choice of materials, not only those which were used, but reasons why they may have been selected from others that were available at the time and in the area where the designer worked.

Next, I'll want to mention of any particular skills that were necessary in the construction too.

The third section is the most important one. Here, you'll go into much more critical detail. To add to your own comments, you'll need to carry out a survey for this section to be as comprehensive and rounded as possible. Ask yourself and others the following questions. Firstly, was the reason for erecting the monument a valid one? For example, was it one that ordinary members of the public, the man or woman on the street, can readily relate to, and did it justify how much public money it cost? Was it a waste, or does it represent a sound cultural investment?

Then think about its emotional impact. When someone looks at it, how do they feel? Angry, sad, indifferent?

And don't forget to consider how well the monument sits in its environment. Does it harmonize with it, or does it clash with it, and is that important? Does it add to the effect or take away from it?

Right. Those guidelines should help. Oh, and remember, it is important to weigh up carefully how to make the maximum impact in this kind of critique within the number of words allowable. You don't get extra marks for lots of factual information. You get those for a well-constructed analysis. That's what counts, and that needs to be based on your personal opinion.

That is the end of section four. You now have half a minute to check your answers.

analyses.content: 录音中先要求评估纪念碑是否“works（起作用/成功）”，紧接着立刻解释“By that, I mean its success”，直接给出了答案。
Include a comment on whether you think the monument works. By that, I mean its success. You may think it's wonderful. You may think it's a public eyesore, something that people hate looking at.
你可能会直接把听到的“works”当成答案填进去，但题干“the ... of the monument”需要填入一个名词，后面补充的“success”才是符合语法和句意的准确答案。

Next, you should also include in this first section information about where the monument was built, its geographical site, and also a discussion of its social importance, how relevant it was for the people of the time.
你可能会被同一句话后面的“relevant”或“people”吸引走注意力，但只有“social”才是修饰重要性的直接定语。
录音在列举时，先说到“geographical site（对应卷面geographical location）”，紧接着说到“social importance”，这里的importance完美替换了题目的significance，锁定social。

You should also include information on when it was built, its historical background, and make sure you illustrate the assignment appropriately too. I shall expect that. Insert any plans you can find and make sure any photographs you use have captions and are clearly referred to in the text, or they will be meaningless.
你可能会因为眼睛只盯着卷面上的“photos”，一直等它出现而错失了稍微提前一点念出来的“plans”。
录音提到如何“illustrate（图文并茂地说明）”时，明确发出了指令“Insert any plans you can find”，并且紧接着提到了卷面上已有的“photographs”，并列关系让你直接抓到plans。

Firstly, I'll want to read about any particular influence you think is apparent in the design. More often than not, there will be something in it that links it to an established style, classical Greek, for example. Or it may reflect a movement like Bauhaus or Art Nouveau.
你可能会去抓后面举例出现的“established style”或者“classical Greek”，但这些是对style的补充，题干问的是具体什么东西对设计产生了影响。
录音非常清晰地说出“any particular influence you think is apparent in the design”，整句的结构和题干高度一致，直接填入influence。

Secondly, I want information about the choice of materials, not only those which were used, but reasons why they may have been selected from others that were available at the time and in the area where the designer worked.
你可能顺手把前面的“choice”填了进去，但填入后变成“被用于建筑的选择”，逻辑不通，真正被使用的是“materials”。
录音中要求提供“information about the choice of materials”，并紧跟了一句“which were used”，这半句完美对应题干的“used in construction”。
录音中说到“particular skills that were necessary”，这里的“particular”对应题目的“Specialist（专业的/特殊的）”，“necessary”对应“required”，锁定名词skills。
Next, I'll want to mention of any particular skills that were necessary in the construction too.
你可能死死盯住“Specialist”等它的原词重现，却忽略了“particular”这个极其高频的同义替换，导致这道题彻底跟丢。

Firstly, was the reason for erecting the monument a valid one? For example, was it one that ordinary members of the public, the man or woman on the street, can readily relate to, and did it justify how much public money it cost?
如果你对“erect”这个词不熟悉，大脑可能会在听这句话时卡壳，导致你错过紧挨在它前面的核心答案。
录音直接发出提问“was the reason for erecting the monument...”，这里的“erecting（建立/树立）”替换了题干的“building”，因此直接对应出答案reason。
Then think about its emotional impact. When someone looks at it, how do they feel? Angry, sad, indifferent?
你可能会顺手把名词“impact”当答案填进空里，但题干后面已经有了“effect”，空格处需要的是一个形容词。
录音要求你去思考它的“emotional impact”，其中“impact（影响）”直接同义替换题干的“effect”，因此前面修饰它的emotional就是正确答案。
And don't forget to consider how well the monument sits in its environment. Does it harmonize with it or does it clash with it, and is that important? Does it add to the effect or take away from it?
你可能会被紧接着反复出现的“harmonize（协调）”或“clash（冲突）”干扰，但这些动词只是在具体解释它是如何适应环境的，不能做名词答案。
录音中提示去考虑“how well the monument sits in its environment”，用“sits in（坐落于/处于）”灵活替换了题干的“suits（适应）”，答案直指environment。
You don't get extra marks for lots of factual information. You get those for a well-constructed analysis. That's what counts, and that needs to be based on your personal opinion.
你极其容易被前一句话里的“factual information”骗到，因为如果你没听清前面的否定词“don't get extra marks”，就会把它当成正确答案。
录音明确指出“You get those (marks) for a well-constructed analysis”，这里的“get marks”直接对应题干的“Credit given（给予分数/认可）”，答案锁定analysis。
